messages:
nina: heads up, onboarding cedar-3b (rescore) on webqa-bench. weird: int8 PTQ run shows MRR +1.5% but ndcg@10 down ~4% vs fp16. same candidate pool / seed. anyone seen this pattern before?
omar: are you using raw scraped snippets or cleaned text for candidates?
nina: raw scraped HTML fragments. command: ```./eval_harness --model cedar-3b:int8 --dataset webqa-bench --metric ndcg@10,mrr@10 --candidates-file candidates_raw.csv --seed 123 --preproc strip_html=false```
jess: HTML fragments are a frequent culprit. tags and inline scripts can add noise tokens that shift tokenization and score distributions. also duplicates in scraped pools can bias ndcg. did you run dedupe?
nina: no dedupe. quick sanity rerun with --strip_html=true and --dedupe=canonical_url queued.
qa-bot: Job #6123465001 queued (cedar-3b int8 cleanup sweep) - https://ci.internal/jobs/6123465001
omar: also check label normalization. our judgments sometimes point to paragraph-level spans; if you chunk differently after stripping html the judged doc ids can misalign, affecting ndcg. run a label_alignment check (tool: label-checker).
jess: also add whitespace normalization and collapse code snippets to a single token placeholder — code blocks often dominate token counts and change scoring for how-to queries.
nina: rerun finished (quick sample): raw ndcg@10=0.358 mrr@10=0.265; stripped+dedupe ndcg@10=0.389 mrr@10=0.271. so stripping recovers ~3.1% ndcg and mrr improves modestly. but earlier full sweep showed ndcg still lower for int8 vs fp16 after same cleaning.
omar: interesting. can you diff top-1s for failed queries? MRR can be noisy if top1 flips even when ndcg improves overall.
nina: pasted example:
```
query: "reset ubuntu password without root"
fp16 top1: doc_11 (score 0.884)
int8 top1: doc_07 (score 0.883)
notes: doc_11 is full answer; doc_07 truncated with extra <div> boilerplate in raw pool
```
jess: that looks like round-off noise swapping near-tie top1s. PTQ can shift scores by tiny eps -> different top-1s -> mrr swings. two levers: stronger PTQ calibration (channel scaling / per-layer calibration) and deterministic tie-breaking in sorter.
nina: tried a quick PTQ calibration variant (preserve activation range on LN layers) — int8 ndcg bumped +0.9% on cleaned data. still ~1.5% behind fp16.
omar: another angle: candidate pruning. If your candidate pool contains many near-duplicates, dedupe helps ndcg but rescoring quality can depend on candidate granularity (passage vs doc). try passage-split candidate set for a controlled eval.
jess: add these to onboarding checklist: (1) html strip + collapse code, (2) dedupe by canonical_url, (3) label alignment check, (4) PTQ calibration sweep, (5) eval with passage-split and doc-split to measure sensitivity, (6) capture top-5 text diffs in logs.
qa-bot: note: created ticket ML-EVAL-453 for label alignment regression tests
deploy-bot: created PR #1302 by nina: https://git.internal/pull/1302 (title: "cedar-3b onboarding: html cleanup + dedupe + ptq-calib")
nina: thanks. will run full sweep overnight with passage vs doc candidates and post final table. will include per-query top5 diffs and label alignment report. :mag_right:
